content:
A growing number of users have recently complained that their Macs are showing the rainbow spinning wheel when running macOS 26.5, with some reporting that their trackpad becomes completely unresponsive for several seconds.

Activity Monitor typically shows three processes causing the issue, and a reliable fix now appears to have been found…

I mentioned this issue last month, speculating that it might be related to the Apple Intelligence image scanning feature. Looking at Activity Monitor, you will usually find that one, two, or three processes are using an extremely high amount of CPU.

Macworld's Michael Simon is one of the sufferers.

He tried various methods without success before finally finding one that worked: deleting the ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight folder. This of course means that the Mac needs to rebuild its Spotlight index, but he said the problem did not recur after two weeks. My own usage time is less than a day so far, but I have not encountered the same issue either.

If you are willing to wait for Spotlight data to be rebuilt, here is how to delete the data:

  • Open a Finder window
  • Choose Go to Folder… from the Go menu
  • Paste: ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight
  • Press CMD-A to select all, then right-click on any item and choose Move to Trash/Bin
  • Right-click on the Trash/Bin and choose Empty Trash/Bin
  • Confirm the action when prompted

If you have been suffering from this issue, please let us know in the comments whether this method works for you too.
